thread_text:
Maya: Quick thread 1: debating p95 visual options for the route heatmap. Two concepts: a thin dashed p95 line vs a shaded 'ribbon' showing estimated confidence. Sketches: https://redwood-internal.screens/line-vs-ribbon.png
Alex: Ribbon is clearer about uncertainty but can hide hotspots. Leaning to ribbon-on-hover and thin line by default.
Janet: Accessibility first: any overlay must meet contrast or use a patterned fill fallback. If ribbon opacity makes contrast <4.5:1, switch to hatch.
Ravi: UX concern: in small-multiples, ribbon fills will overlap and create visual noise. Default to per-panel scaling and compact line for small panels <240px high.
Maya: Copy idea: control label "p95 (estimate  sampling affects accuracy)" with tooltip: "Estimated tail latency based on sampled requests." Avoid jargon.
Alex: Timepicker keyboard nudge suggestion: left/right to shift by current granularity, shift+arrows for larger steps, and "+"/"-" to expand/contract range. Add aria-describedby to show current granularity.
Janet: Low sample UX: if sample <8% show a dimmed ribbon and an inline badge "Low sample  p95 uncertain". If <3% hide ribbon and show quick action: "Increase sampling".
Ravi: High-throughput edge-case: if routes >10k rps apply log color scale automatically and show a tiny badge "log scale" with ability to toggle linear.
DesignBot: CSS hint: `.p95-line{ stroke-dasharray:3,3; stroke-width:2px; filter: drop-shadow(0 0 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.18)); } .p95-ribbon{ fill: rgba(38,132,255,0.12); }`
Maya: Interaction detail: animate ribbon expand over 220ms on hover; show one-time helper tooltip "Ribbon = estimated p95 range (sampling affects accuracy)".
Alex: Legend voiceover: keyboard focus should read "p95 overlay, visible, sample rate 12%". Janet, can you add this to ARIA spec?
Janet: Yup I'll add aria-labels and an `aria-live` region for sample changes. Also recommend 3px focus ring on toggles.
Ravi: I'll update figma frames with both line + ribbon states and include hatch fallback. ETA 5pm PT and will post link here.
Maya: Great, will review and drop comments. :thumbsup:
